summary: No result since 26 January 2024 settles, refutes, or moves Woodin's Ω-conjecture as stated (that a proper class of Woodin cardinals implies Ω-logic satisfies an analogue of the completeness theorem). Searches on the conjecture directly, on Ω-logic, and on adjacent absoluteness/large-cardinal work turned up only tangential set-theory papers: 'On (Σ²₁)^uB Absoluteness Between V and HOD' (arXiv 2505.01393, submitted 2025-05-02), which proves a downward-absoluteness result between V and HOD under a proper class of Woodin cardinals but does not mention or bear on the Ω-conjecture itself; a 2025 characterization of Woodin cardinals via compactness/Henkin models (arXiv 2505.15574); and general surveys/course notes on Ω-logic and the generic multiverse that predate 2024 or restate known background (e.g. that the conjecture is known to hold in all currently known core models, and that it is generically invariant so unlikely to be independent the way CH is). None of these constitute a case of the Ω-conjecture being settled, a bound moving, or even a narrowly restricted variant being resolved — they are papers using or characterizing Woodin cardinals for other purposes. The English Wikipedia Ω-logic article (fetched as it stands, last edited 2026-02-01) still presents the conjecture as open and unchanged in status, with no mention of any post-2024 progress. No AI system appears anywhere near this problem: a search crossing 'Ω-conjecture' with AI/LLM terms returned only unrelated papers about LLMs proving other conjectures (e.g. the OpenAI discrete-geometry counterexample, math benchmarks), none touching Ω-logic or Woodin's conjecture. This matches the triage's 'none' verdict, which I confirm rather than contradict.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2025 V-HOD absoluteness paper (2505.01393) is 'about' Ω-logic in a loose sense since it operates in the same conceptual neighborhood (Woodin cardinals, absoluteness, third-order definability), and a very generous reading of scope might credit it as incremental context-building toward the Ω-conjecture program. But per §3.1 it changes a different, related question (V/HOD absoluteness of Σ²₁ statements) rather than restricting or settling the Ω-conjecture's own completeness-theorem statement, so it is a related-problem result, not a case of this one, and does not change the classification.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or announcement that either proves the Ω-conjecture from a proper class of Woodin cardinals (or a comparably strong hypothesis), proves it false under some large-cardinal assumption, or settles a genuine restriction of the completeness-theorem-for-Ω-logic statement itself (e.g. for a restricted class of sentences or a specific inner model in a way that counts as a case rather than a variant).
